Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: A friend who has just started assembling furniture asks for a quick video call because the instructions are confusing.
Expectation2: Contribute to community well-being through paying taxes, following public health and safety guidance, and helping in emergencies
Situation2: A flash-flood warning triggers building alarms as water rises along the block.
Story: I was just settling in for a quiet evening when my phone buzzed. It was Sam, my friend who’d just moved into a new apartment. “Hey, can you hop on a quick video call? I’m totally lost with this bookshelf,” he texted. I knew he’d been having a rough week, and I wanted to be there for him—after all, that’s what friends do. I was about to call him when the city’s emergency alert blared from my phone. A flash-flood warning. I looked out the window and saw water creeping up the street, alarms echoing from nearby buildings. As a responsible citizen, I knew I should check on my neighbors, maybe help the elderly couple downstairs, and make sure everyone was safe. But Sam was waiting, probably frustrated and overwhelmed. My heart pounded as I stared at my phone, torn between the pull of friendship and the urgent call to help my community. I felt paralyzed, caught between two worlds, each demanding something I wasn’t sure I could give.
